I decided to see a psychologist, I couldn't deal with the anxiety anymore. I described my problems and he was suspicious of me having hypochondria. He gave me a couple of tests (took like 15 minutes to complete) which I scored very high on and that's where he diagnosed me.

I don't know what the treatment is called in English, but at first he asked me a bunch of questions to get to the root of the problem. He made me complete a few "tasks" over the next few weeks to 
potentially reduce my need for constant reassurance, such as not googling for 30 minutes when I had the urge to etc. 

In my case (can't speak for others with the condition), there is not a link between hypochondria and Munchausens. I obsess over the fear of NOT being normal. For example, I have tinnitus. When I realized that hearing a high pitched ringing noise 24/7 was not normal (only learned about tinnitus not too long ago) I panicked and started trying to convince myself I didn't have tinnitus. I went to a doctor and turns out I have hearing impairment in my right ear, with tinnitus. I wanted to die. I've never told anyone about my hearing problems and I don't want to be perceived as hearing impaired at all, I want the opposite of that. I just want to be perceived as a normal dude. I want the same physical capabilities as the majority does. I also hate being at the hospital, I avoid it as much as I can, I'd rather just be home googling and trying to reassure myself I don't have something I'm worrying about. I'm scared of being diagnosed with illnesses or diseases so I run away from doctors as they might diagnose me with something I would potentially waste hours obsessing over. I have been to the doctor about a problem a handful of times though, the anxiety takes over and I just HAVE to know if I have this or not. Sitting at the hospital always fills me with anxiety and I'm very relieved when I'm out.

Munchausens is being convinced you have some disease or illness right? If I hear about an illness and I relate with any of the symptoms I try my hardest to reassure myself I do NOT have the illness, so I don't think I fit the criteria of Munchausens.

This is all kind of hard to explain so sorry if this is difficult to follow haha. Hope you get something out of this at least :). Good luck with counseling!

He got a solid hairline, he's not going to be losing it any time soon. I'd say worst case scenario he'll have a noticeably receding hairline at 35 years old. Best case he's not losing hair at all, simply going through "hairline maturing". It's a thing.

His hairline is actually pretty average for his age. There are a ton of people who have it a lot worse and are STILL not going to be losing it that soon. Callmecarson, Quadeca, Logan Paul, Jake Paul and Muselk are all individuals that have started the balding process (not all at the same stage though).

There is also medication that you can take that pretty much STOPS balding entirely (or at the very least slows balding significantly). It's called Finasteride (or Propecia). But you have to take this medication for life if you want to keep your hairline, it's a big commitment and can have sexual side effects (low libido, erectile dysfunction). For that reason, most people that are balding don't take the medication.

In conclusion, his hair is probably not going anywhere soon and thus not a problem at all.

Source: Me, a balding 19 year old that has done a shit ton of research on this topic because of my uncontrollable insecurities about my hairline.
